description: Recognise and manage a hypertensive emergency per the 2026 ISH Global Hypertension Practice Guidelines — distinguish emergency (very high BP with acute organ damage) from asymptomatic severe hypertension, the clinical presentations (malignant hypertension, encephalopathy, thrombotic microangiopathy, stroke, ACS, pulmonary oedema, aortic dissection, severe preeclampsia/eclampsia), the investigations, and the timeline, BP target and first-line IV drug for each presentation. Use when a clinician asks "BP 220/130 what to do", "is this hypertensive emergency or urgency", "how fast to lower BP", "IV antihypertensive choice", "BP target in acute stroke", "BP in aortic dissection", "labetalol or nicardipine", "malignant hypertension management", or "BP lowering in ischaemic stroke before thrombolysis". Source: Stergiou GS et al, 2026 ISH Global Hypertension Practice Guidelines, J Hypertens 2026 (DOI 10.1097/HJH.0000000000004451).
